exceptions.title: renders content passed through the render prop
exceptions.reason: The case gives its content in the React element of `render`, and the part reads the children of that element. A Vue part cannot read what its `#render` slot renders. It renders only while it has a default slot or the content of its toast.

exceptions.title: does not sync provider props from an abandoned render
exceptions.reason: The case suspends a React transition, and React then abandons a render. Vue has no render that it abandons.
The file imports `Dialog` from the entry point of Dialog, which Vase UI does not have. Each case renders parts of `Dialog`.

exceptions.title: requires an element whose children are renderable
exceptions.reason: The case builds React elements. A Vue part cannot read the children of a vnode, so Vase UI has no `hasRenderableChildren`. The cases of the label parts test the rule that replaces it: a part renders only while it has a default slot or a label with content.

returnTypeDifferences.reason: The source of Base UI returns the same type, `ToastManager<Data>`. Its `types.md` prints the type argument as `{}`.

`setup` runs one time, so a plain array does not follow a change of the toasts. `toasts` of the result is thus a `ComputedRef` of the array. The source of Base UI returns `UseToastManagerReturnValue<Data>`, and its `types.md` prints the type argument as `{}`.
